styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Classical gardens, silk and the old canal lanes.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Temples, museums and 2,500 years of city life.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Gardens, canals and lakeside walks outside town.

stays.why: Central shopping street; walk to the Humble Administrator's Garden and the museum. Busy and easy for first-timers.
Canal-side lanes with teahouses and small inns. The most atmospheric base for evening walks.
Modern hotels, the lakefront and easy metro. Good value and quiet, but 20–30 minutes from the old town.
Cheapest and best for early trains to Shanghai; short metro ride to the gardens.

food: Try Suzhou classics: squirrel-shaped mandarin fish, braised pork belly and sweet red-braised dishes. The local taste is sweeter than most Chinese food.
Suzhou-style noodles for breakfast: a bowl of soup noodles with toppings costs about ¥15–30.
Teahouses on Pingjiang Road serve local green tea; expect ¥50–100 per person for tea and snacks.
Crab season is roughly October to November; hairy crab is pricey, so check the price per liang before ordering.
Street snacks in the old lanes: sweet rice cakes, osmanthus sweets and small dumplings, mostly ¥5–20.
more_time: Add a day trip to Tongli or Zhouzhuang water towns: buses and trains run from Suzhou, about 1 hour each way. Check times on the day.
Shanghai is about 30 minutes by high-speed train. A half-day trip is easy from Suzhou Station.
Garden fans can swap one garden for the Master of the Nets Garden evening show, or add Tiger Hill and Hanshan Temple in one morning.

recommend.why: Two nights let you see the main gardens, the old canals and the museum without rushing, and still fit a water-town side trip.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 9°C, lows near 1°C. Pack a warm coat; gardens are quiet.
Still chilly, highs around 11°C. Few crowds and low hotel prices.
Warming up to 16°C with about 11 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
One of the best months: 21°C highs, gardens green and blooming.
Warm and pleasant at 26°C. Good for walking the canals.
Hot and wet: 28°C highs, 16 rain days. Plan indoor sights midday.
Hottest month, highs near 32°C and humid. Go out early or late.
Hot and humid again, around 32°C. Carry water.
Cooling to 28°C. Comfortable again, with about 12 rain days.
Excellent month: 23°C highs, dry-ish and clear. Crab season starts.
Mild at 18°C. Good light for gardens and photos.
Cold again at 11°C highs, but only about 7 rain days. Quiet streets.

climate_guide.summary: Humid subtropical: hot, wet summers and cool, fairly dry winters. Spring and autumn are the best times to visit.

items.title: Best time: April to May and October to November
items.text: Highs of 21–26°C and 23°C in October. Comfortable for gardens and canal walks.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid (June to August)
items.text: Highs of 28–32°C with 14–16 rain days. Sightsee early morning; rest indoors at midday.

items.title: Rain peaks in June and July
items.text: About 16 rain days each month. Pack a light raincoat and shoes that dry fast.

items.title: Winter is cool, not freezing
items.text: January highs near 9°C and lows near 1°C. Rarely snows, but damp cold feels sharp; bring a warm layer.

items.title: Spring rain
items.text: March and April each have about 11 rain days. An umbrella is worth carrying.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for spring and autumn, a warm coat for December to February, and rain gear for summer. Comfortable shoes for garden paths.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; Didi or taxi for gardens and evenings.

modes.text: 9 lines; lines 1 and 4 cross downtown. Fares ¥2–6. Fast and cheap for the old town and the station.
Buses run 05:00–21:00 every 10–20 min. Most fares ¥1–2; exact change needed. Tourist buses Y1–Y5 link the railway station and main sights.
Taxis flag ¥10 for 3 km, then about ¥3.2/km. Use the queue, not touts. Didi works well; few drivers speak English, so show Chinese addresses.
Not worth it for a short visit. Traffic and parking in the old town are hard; use metro and taxis instead.
Fine downtown and along the canals. Bikes rent for about ¥30/day; keep bikes locked.
